_source: Godot: player_controller_3d.gd 1923-1935 (clip choice), remote_players.gd 736-763 and 1194-1215 (remote clip + pace), model_slot.gd 444 (crouch fade), player_stride.gd + hunter_stride.gd (pace). Read by render/anim/runner.rs.
_wire: The pose name a runner's net sample carries (`clip`, Godot remote_players.gd `clip`): state key -> wire name. A sample with no name (an older client) is read from its moving, sprinting and crouching flags.
_swim: Rust-only (the Godot rig has no swim clip): deep water plays the walk clip at the real swim pace and leans the body forward by pitch_deg about the hips (pivot_m above the feet), easing at pitch_rate per second.
_head: The head turns in the body's frame (the rig's Head bone): up and down follows the runner's aim pitch, clamped to pitch_limit_deg; left and right first follows the aim yaw (the facing) relative to the body, clamped to aim_yaw_limit_deg, plus a small lag behind the body's turns (the head trails a turn by yaw_lag_s seconds of turn rate, clamped to yaw_limit_deg). Both ease at smoothing per second. Down, stunned and climbing runners hold the head straight.
_body: The body follows the head (head-first look). The head turns alone while the aim is within the free range: still_free_deg standing, moving_free_deg walking or sprinting. Past it, the body turns after follow_delay_s seconds of overshoot, easing at follow_smoothing per second, until the head is back at the free range.
_jump: The remote jump pose: the jump clip is played over the runner's real airtime, not in time. A runner's wire jump height (metres above its floor) maps onto the clip through peak_m, the height the jump peaks at (keep it equal to the jump's peak in data/player/jump.json): the rise plays the first half of the clip, the fall the second half.
_crouch: Crouching plays IDLE (the imported crouch pose folds knees and elbows backward) and fades the body to this alpha; fade_rate is move_toward units per second.

stride._note: References at authored size (assets/hunters_blocky/stride_table.json, player_mannequin); the rig's own stride table wins when it has the clip. Multiplied by model_scale (PlayerModels.SCALE).
